public.prompt: A flex row has a fixed-width sidebar and `.main { flex: 1; }`. One unbreakable filename makes `.main` wider than the remaining space. Which declaration directly allows that flex item to shrink below its automatic content minimum?

options.label: Set `.main { width: 100%; }` so the item claims the row width before the sidebar is reserved.
Set `.main { min-width: 0; }` so its used width may fall below the content-based minimum.
Set `.main { flex-shrink: 0; }` so the item preserves the filename's intrinsic width during layout.

answerProof.summary: Setting the flex item's minimum width to zero lets it shrink below the automatic content-based minimum within the space left by the sidebar.
decisiveConstraints: The main flex item must be allowed below its automatic content-based minimum.

claims.statement: Flex items can use an automatic content-based minimum width, and setting min-width zero permits the item to shrink further.

optionRationales.explanation: A 100% main width consumes the row before the fixed sidebar is accounted for and does not remove the automatic minimum size.
optionRationales.plausibility: A percentage width appears to constrain the main area to the viewport.
optionRationales.falsifyingConstraint: The main item must shrink within the space left after the fixed sidebar.

optionRationales.explanation: The zero minimum lets the main item shrink within the space that remains after the fixed sidebar.
Disabling shrink preserves the oversized intrinsic width and makes row overflow more likely.
optionRationales.plausibility: Preventing shrink can protect content from being visually compressed.
optionRationales.falsifyingConstraint: The main item must be allowed to shrink below its content-based minimum.
